title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 14
statement: For a set of four distinct lines in a plane, there are exactly \(N\) distinct points that lie on two or more of the lines. What is the sum of all possible values of \(N?\)

solutions.text:
The values \(0,1,3,4,5,\) and \(6\) are attainable. Four parallel lines give \(0\), four concurrent lines give \(1\), three parallel lines cut by a fourth give \(3\), three concurrent lines plus a fourth not through that point give \(4\), three lines forming a triangle plus a fourth parallel to one side give \(5\), and four lines in general position give \(\binom42=6\).

It remains to rule out \(2\). Choose two nonparallel lines, meeting at \(X\). If a third line also passes through \(X\), then a fourth line not through \(X\) intersects at least two of those three concurrent lines at two different new points; otherwise all four lines pass through \(X\), giving only one point. If the third line does not pass through \(X\), then to create only one new point it must be parallel to one of the first two lines. A fourth distinct line cannot pass through either existing intersection without meeting the parallel line at a new point, and if it passes through neither, it creates a new intersection immediately. Thus exactly two intersection points are impossible.

Thus the possible values are \(0,1,3,4,5,6\), whose sum is \(19\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: List attainable intersection counts for four lines
Then separately rule out exactly two intersection points
